rows.notes: [jp] "Suke-san" (not in glossary). Kept ambiguity resolved: [jp] could grammatically mean the prince is the one fond of proverbs; read as describing the tutor.

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Suke-san
%4■Full Name■%1
Duke Skade
%4■Profile■%1
> A young man accompanying Prince Mito as an attendant on his tour of inspection.
> Prince Mito's tutor, who loves quoting proverbs and maxims.
> He has his hands full with the prince, who is always trying to skip his studies.
> He can be serious and stiff, but he is an understanding person.
{x00}
rows.notes: [jp] "Suke-san" (not in glossary). Kept ambiguity resolved: [jp] could grammatically mean the prince is the one fond of proverbs; read as describing the tutor.

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Kaku-san
%4■Full Name■%1
Baron Karcus
%4■Profile■%1
> A young man accompanying Prince Mito as an attendant on his tour of inspection.
> Prince Mito's tutor, who instructs him in swordsmanship.
> As a martial artist, he seems to be fairly well known in the Ipron system.
> Careless about details by nature, a big eater and very strong.
{x00}
rows.notes: [jp] "Kaku-san" (not in glossary). | [accuracy] [jp] = loose, not attentive to detail; "easygoing" ([jp]) softened it | [editorial] accuracy flag: 'rough-and-ready' reads as praise; [jp] = not attentive to detail

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Kaku-san
%4■Full Name■%1
Baron Karcus
%4■Profile■%1
> A young man accompanying Prince Mito as an attendant on his tour of inspection.
> Prince Mito's tutor, who instructs him in swordsmanship.
> As a martial artist, he seems to be fairly well known in the Ipron system.
> Careless about details by nature, a big eater and very strong.
{x00}
rows.notes: [jp] "Kaku-san" (not in glossary).

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Shinobu
%4■Full Name■%1
Flora Shinobu
%4■Profile■%1
> A girl in charge of Prince Mito's personal protection and intelligence gathering.
> In the Edon homeland she served as bodyguard to the queen, Prince Mito's mother.
> Though young, she is a skilled martial artist, good with machines and nimble.
> She pines for the prince, but believing their difference in status makes it hopeless, she cannot bring herself to voice her feelings.
{x00}
rows.notes: [accuracy] [jp] = yearns / pines for; "is in love with" weakened it

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Baljang
%4■Profile■%1
> Chief retainer of the Edon Kingdom and Prince Mito's watchful minder.
> He was the prince's guardian when the prince was little, and is the person Prince Mito finds hardest to deal with.
> He fusses over Prince Mito to an extreme degree, and when the prince left on his tour of inspection without telling him, he set out on a journey himself to chase after the prince.
> Whenever something goes wrong, he tries to take responsibility by committing seppuku.
> He is afraid of dogs.
{x00}

%4■Name■%1
Ryan
%4■Profile■%1
> Prince Mito's childhood friend.
{x00}
rows.notes: Source line has no final period; one added.

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Wataru
%4■Full Name■%1
Wataru Ikusabe
%4■Profile■%1
> An energetic fourth-grader.
> By an odd twist of fate he is summoned to Sokaizan, another world, where he fights evil as the Savior to restore peace.
> He loves playing, from video games to baseball, but he really hates studying.
> He detests lies and bullying of the weak, and he is the type who cannot let bad guys get away with anything.
{x00}
rows.notes: Doakudar/Sokaizan/Savior not in glossary; romanized (Sokaizan) / translated (Savior).

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Toraoh
%4■Real Name■%1
Shoryushi
%4■Profile■%1
> The son of Doakudar, the emperor of evil.
> He is so mischievous and hates losing so much that even his closest aides have trouble handling him.
> Wataru and the others do not know this, and Toraoh does not know that Wataru is the Savior and his father's enemy.
> He is fond of Himiko and says, "I'm gonna make her my bride!" but he is thought not to understand what the word "bride" means.
> In truth he is Shoryushi, son of Seiryuhi, the goddess of Sokaizan, whom Doakudar has imprisoned in order to rule Sokaizan.
{x00}
rows.notes: New header label [jp] = "Real Name". Doakudar, Shoryushi, Seiryuhi romanized (not in glossary). "Ore-sama" swagger rendered as "I'm gonna". | [proofread] punctuation: comma after a closing quote that ends in "!" removed

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Himiko
%4■Full Name■%1
Himiko Shinobibe
%4■Profile■%1
> A girl from Monja Village at the foot of Sokaizan, who travels with Wataru.
> Though only 7 years old, she is the 13th head of the Shinobibe clan, and gets through one crisis after another with her outlandish ninja arts.
> She has a bottomless stomach and boundless energy; she has no worries and is afraid of nothing.
> She is always running around here and there, her laughter ringing out.
{x00}
rows.notes: Monja Village romanized (not in glossary).

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Shibaraku
%4■Full Name■%1
Shibaraku Tsurugibe
%4■Profile■%1
> A master swordsman of the Yagyu Shibaraku style, a two-sword school.
> With the X-Cut, a deadly special move, Shibaraku cuts down villains left and right.
> To Wataru, Shibaraku is a good teacher, whom he calls "Sensei."
> Warm-hearted, Shibaraku values friends above all else, but is utterly helpless against beautiful women and rock-paper-scissors.
> Currently looking for a bride.
{x00}
rows.notes: Glossary gender null and the text has no pronoun, so no he/she used. [jp] (yagyu, "wild ox") romanized as Yagyu, losing the pun. [jp] = "X-Cut" (glossary note: X-cut slash). Last line kept subjectless (source is a terse tagline: [jp]). | [editorial] name-repetition/passive smoothed (Wataru is male per glossary)

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Kurama
%4■Full Name■%1
Kurama Wataribe
%4■Profile■%1
> A young man turned into a bird by the curse of Doakudar, the emperor of evil who holds Sokaizan in his grip.
> To get his original form back, he approached Wataru and the others as a spy, but he was moved by their friendship and joined them.
> Though he constantly complains that Wataru and the others are too soft, he ends up helping them anyway; he has a caring side.
> Himiko always calls him "Mr. Bird."
{x00}

%4■Name■%1
Ryujinmaru
%4■Profile■%1
> A Mashin born when the Golden Dragon possessed a clay robot that Wataru made in arts-and-crafts class.
> The Mashin not only has a will of its own, of course, but can also converse freely.
> In battle, naturally, and elsewhere too, he scolds and encourages Wataru as a good mentor in life.
{x00}
rows.notes: [jp] = "Mashin", [jp] = "Golden Dragon" (not in glossary). Source switches from [jp] to [jp]; kept "its" for the Mashin itself and "he" for the later sentence as in the source.

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Spike
%4■Full Name■%1
Spike Spiegel
%4■Profile■%1
> A bounty hunter -- a "cowboy," as they are called -- who roams all over the Earth sphere.
> A master of the martial art called "Jeet Kune Do."
> He loves money, but it never seems to come his way, and he does not seem all that attached to it either.
> In the past he belonged to the Martian mafia syndicate "Red Dragon," and he lives constantly putting himself in danger.
{x00}
rows.notes: [jp] kept literal as "Earth sphere". Red Dragon, Jeet Kune Do per official English usage.

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Jet
%4■Full Name■%1
Jet Black
%4■Profile■%1
> A bounty hunter and the owner of the Bebop, an interplanetary ship converted from a used fishing boat.
> Stubborn, loyal and single-minded, he is clumsy but holds fast to his idea of how a man should live.
> Aboard the Bebop he mainly handles maintenance and cooking, and his hobby is bonsai.
> He was formerly a police officer with the ISSP (Inter Solar System Police).
> Due to an accident during his time on the force, his left arm has been replaced with a prosthetic.
{x00}
rows.notes: ISSP gloss "Inter Solar System Police" (official Bebop English; source gloss is literally "Solar System Criminal Police Organization").

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Faye
%4■Full Name■%1
Faye Valentine
%4■Profile■%1
> A female bounty hunter who, through a chance turn of events, settled in aboard the Bebop.
> Because of an accident she spent over 50 years in cold sleep, and she has lost her memories of the time before.
> As a result she was swindled by a con man and saddled with an enormous debt, so her obsession with money is extraordinary.
> A self-centered, shrewd realist, she cares about nothing except money.
> Her hobby is gambling, and her special skill is cheating.
{x00}

%4■Name■%1
Ed
%4■Full Name■%1
Edward Wong Hau Pepelu Tivrusky IV
%4■Profile■%1
> A genius hacker who can access any data.
> A creature of whim, doing whatever she likes, whenever and however she likes.
> A self-proclaimed 13-year-old whose thoughts are impossible to read, and whose words and actions are almost those of a wild animal.
> She forced her way aboard the Bebop and now freeloads there.
> She can understand what Ein, the genius dog kept aboard the Bebop, is saying.
{x00}
rows.notes: Glossary gender null and the text has no pronoun, so none used. The two-line full name joined on one line. Spelling Pepelu/Tivrusky per glossary note. | [editorial] Ed is female (project decision): name-repetition workarounds replaced with she/her

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Ein
%4■Profile■%1
> A genius dog kept aboard the Bebop.
{x00}

%4■Name■%1
Ryo
%4■Full Name■%1
Ryo Sanada
%4■Profile■%1
> A Samurai Trooper with the heart of "Benevolence," who fights clad in the Yoroi Gear of Rekka.
> He comes from the Sanada ninja corps of Shinshu.
> Learning that the human world was coming under threat from the Yoja, he came to join the fight together with Byakuen, a white tiger.
> Perhaps because he grew up deep in the mountains, he is poor at dealing with people and not much of a talker, but he is an honest, gentle boy who loves nature and can sense its heart.
> However, he is somewhat stubborn, and often charges ahead without listening when those around him try to stop him, only to run into a wall.
{x00}
rows.notes: [jp] ([jp]) = "Yoroi Gear" (not in glossary; reading-based). [jp] = "Benevolence" (glossary: virtue Jin). Byakuen romanized. Source [jp] read as typo for [jp] (threat).

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Seiji
%4■Full Name■%1
Seiji Date
%4■Profile■%1
> A Samurai Trooper with the heart of "Courtesy," who fights clad in the Yoroi Gear of Korin.
> He comes from Sendai and counts Date Masamune among his ancestors.
> He practices kendo, and his hobbies -- bonsai, traditional Japanese instruments and caring for swords -- are rather old-fashioned.
> He gives the impression of being quiet and cool, but apparently he simply dislikes people and does not like talking.
> Still, he is certainly level-headed, and together with Toma he often steps in to stop Ryo and Shu, who tend to rush ahead at the slightest excuse.
{x00}
rows.notes: Historical name Date Masamune kept in Japanese order. [jp] = "Courtesy".

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Shin
%4■Full Name■%1
Shin Mouri
%4■Profile■%1
> A Samurai Trooper with the heart of "Trust," who fights clad in the Yoroi Gear of Suiko.
> He has a sharp tongue for someone so gentle-looking, but at heart he is mild-tempered and cares about his friends.
> His family runs a Hagi ware pottery kiln, and he comes from the Mouri, an illustrious family descended from Mouri Motonari.
> His hobby is cooking.
{x00}
rows.notes: [jp] = "Trust". Historical Mouri Motonari in Japanese order, spelled Mouri to match the glossary surname.

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Shu
%4■Full Name■%1
Shu Layfang
%4■Profile■%1
> A Samurai Trooper with the heart of "Righteousness," who fights clad in the Yoroi Gear of Kongo.
> He has a strong sense of justice and a single-minded, simple and straightforward personality, but in fact he also has a thoughtful side.
> His family runs a Chinese restaurant in Yokohama, and of the five Samurai Troopers he grew up in the wealthiest home, but he never shows off about it.
> He once suspected that the Samurai Troopers' Yoroi Gear might, in the end, be the same as that of the Four Masho -- a power of destruction -- but at the time he overcame that doubt by believing in their own justice.
{x00}
rows.notes: [jp] = "Righteousness". [jp] = "Four Masho" (built from glossary Oni/Yami/Doku/Gen Masho). | [accuracy] [jp] = simple/uncomplicated, not 'cheerful'; [jp] = single-minded

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Toma
%4■Full Name■%1
Toma Hashiba
%4■Profile■%1
> A Samurai Trooper with the heart of "Wisdom," who fights clad in the Yoroi Gear of Tenku.
> He comes from a family descended from the house of the Taiko-Kanpaku, who unified the realm in the Sengoku period.
> Always calm, composed and sharp-witted, he might be called the strategist of the Samurai Troopers.
> Thoughtful, he rarely puts himself forward; he analyzes situations accurately, restrains Ryo and the others when they tend to run wild, and deftly steers them back on course.
{x00}
rows.notes: [jp] = "Wisdom". [jp] kept as the title "Taiko-Kanpaku" without naming Hideyoshi (source does not name him).

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Shuten
%4■Full Name■%1
Shuten Doji
%4■Real Name■%1
Toshitada Koma
%4■Profile■%1
> One of the Four Masho who serve Arago, the Yoja Emperor; he is the Oni Masho.
> He is the youngest of the Four Masho, but stronger than any other Masho, and holds the top position among them.
> Once a warlord of the Sengoku period, he, like so many at the time, aimed to rule the land, but the domain he was born in was small and weak, and it took all he had just to protect it.
> His frustration at making so little headway was exploited; he was drawn into the Yoja World and made a Masho.
{x00}
rows.notes: [jp] = "Yoja Emperor", [jp] = "Yoja World" (glossary only has Yoja Soldier/Ship/Gate). Real name per glossary note.

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Anubis
%4■Real Name■%1
Kujuro Sasaki
%4■Profile■%1
> One of the Four Masho who serve Arago, the Yoja Emperor; he is the Yami Masho.
> Of all the Masho he has the most single-minded personality, leaning heavily toward martial prowess; in a sense he could also be called a sturdy, upright and sincere man.
{x00}

%4■Name■%1
Naza
%4■Real Name■%1
Naotoki Yamanouchi
%4■Profile■%1
> One of the Four Masho who serve Arago, the Yoja Emperor; he is the Doku Masho.
> Like Rajura, he often resorts to schemes, and he is surprisingly meticulous, putting a good deal of effort into preparing them.
{x00}

%4■Name■%1
Rajura
%4■Real Name■%1
Jirogoro Kuroda
%4■Profile■%1
> One of the Four Masho who serve Arago, the Yoja Emperor; he is the Gen Masho.
> As a master of illusion, he excels at defeating enemies by bewildering them with traps.
> Calm by nature, he is, one could say, the type who is not caught up in small, immediate victories, but slowly drives his opponents into a corner.
{x00}

%4■Name■%1
Kayura
%4■Profile■%1
> A female warrior of the Yoja World.
> She usually resides in the Seireikyu Palace in Bonnokyo, in the Yoja World, wrapped in a junihitoe robe and enjoying Arago's favor.
> Believing the power of the Yoja to be pure, she goes into battle to defeat those who oppose Arago, emperor of the Yoja World.
> Her power is overwhelmingly great, enough to rival even Kikoutei.
> She was originally of the clan of Kaos, which protects the human world from the Yoja, and was its rightful heir.
> However, as a child she was carried off to the Yoja World by Arago, and her memories have been sealed away.
{x00}
rows.notes: Seireikyu, Bonnokyo, Kaos ([jp]) romanized; not in glossary.

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Arago
%4■Profile■%1
> The Yoja Emperor, who rules the Yoja World.
> The source of his power is the emotions of the human world, such as hatred and fear, and his power seems almost limitless.
> Long ago, commanding the Jiryoshu and others, Arago grew in power by defeating rival Masho and the like, and unified the Yoja World.
> He then went on to invade the human world as well, seeking to take it, but that time his ambition was thwarted by Kaos and he was sealed away.
> However, he has built up his power again, revived in the present day, and now burns with new ambition.
{x00}
rows.notes: [editorial] stiff double 'and others' smoothed; 'human-world emotions' clarified

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Toya
%4■Full Name■%1
Toya Shinjo
%4■Profile■%1
> A boy who holds the power of the legendary warrior handed down since ancient times in Eternalia, a world in another dimension.
> Earnest by nature, he tends to brood, and once he does, he can see only one way forward.
> At first glance he is an ordinary high school student, but his parents are inhabitants of Eternalia, a world in a different space-time, and the soul of Radias, that world's legendary warrior, dwells within him.
> However, right after learning this, he was bewildered by the presence of a legendary warrior's soul he knew nothing about, and he denied that the soul existed.
> Even so, as he keeps fighting alongside the Animanoid (beastman) warriors who support him, he gradually becomes aware of his mission and awakens as a Gulkeeva (legendary warrior).
> Peach juice is his favorite.
{x00}
rows.notes: Eternalia, Animanoid romanized (not in glossary). Gulkeeva per glossary series title; Radias per glossary (Sword of Radias). The source's explanatory parentheses ([jp], [jp]) kept as glosses. | [accuracy] [jp] = become aware of (not 'accept') | [editorial] tense clash in one sentence (became ... awakens) made consistent

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Kira
%4■Full Name■%1
Kira Kongo
%4■Profile■%1
> Toya and Konoha's childhood friend, and their best friend.
> Like Toya, he has parents who come from Eternalia, a world in another dimension, and the soul of Lute, a legendary warrior, dwells within him.
> Slender and fine-featured, he looks far from a warrior at first glance, but deep in his heart lie a strong will and the strength to embrace the soul within him.
> Perhaps for that reason, he awakens to the power of the Gulkeeva (legendary warrior) earlier than Toya does.
{x00}
rows.notes: [jp] romanized "Lute" (not in glossary; "Ryuto" also possible). [jp] read as applying to both Toya and Konoha, like [jp].

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Konoha
%4■Full Name■%1
Konoha Maihara
%4■Profile■%1
> Toya and Kira's classmate and childhood friend.
> Cheerful and lively, she loves looking after people, and she is always together with Toya and Kira.
> Her home is a temple called Kintoji, on the outskirts of town.
> For a time Toya, Kira and the Animanoid (beastman) warriors used Kintoji as a hideout, and during that period she took care of all the housework; she has a very domestic side as well.
{x00}
rows.notes: [jp] romanized "Kintoji" (not in glossary). | [editorial] redundant 'classmate at the same school'

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Greyfus
%4■Profile■%1
> A wolf Animanoid (beastman) warrior sent from Eternalia, a world in another dimension, to support Toya.
> He is something of a leader among the Animanoid warriors who were sent, reining Toya in when Toya tries to force his way through with brute strength, and guiding him.
> Usually calm and gentle, he also has a hot-blooded side.
> He is interested in machines and tries to take apart anything and everything.
> Whenever he does, he invariably says, "It's fine, I can fix it," but the odds of a machine he has taken apart actually going back together are low.
> Receiving power from Toya's sword, he becomes the Armored Divine Beast "Kiba."
{x00}
rows.notes: [jp] = "Armored Divine Beast" (not in glossary); Kiba romanized. | [editorial] run-on 'the one who reins Toya in ... and guides him' restructured; 'he' referent clarified

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Beakwood
%4■Profile■%1
> A hawk Animanoid (beastman) warrior sent from Eternalia, a world in another dimension, to support Toya.
> Calm, kind and the type to put logic first, he serves as a kind of strategist among the Animanoid warriors.
> Loving nature and fond of spiritual principles, he often recites poetry and sits in zazen meditation.
> He has shown an interest in Buddhism, and he seems to get along well with Kazuma Maihara, Konoha's father and the head priest of Kintoji.
> Receiving power from Toya's sword, he becomes the Armored Divine Beast "Kiba."
{x00}
rows.notes: [jp] romanized "Kazuma Maihara" (not in glossary; [jp] read Kazuma).

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Garriel
%4■Profile■%1
> A gorilla Animanoid (beastman) warrior sent from Eternalia, a world in another dimension, to support Toya.
> He calls Toya "Chief"; cheerful and bright, he is popular with children too, and he is the one who keeps the Animanoid warriors' spirits up.
> However, partly because of his pure heart, he sometimes ends up weighed down by inner conflict.
> Apparently he gets itchy when a woman touches him, so he is uneasy around women -- though not, it seems, around every woman.
> Receiving power from Toya's sword, he becomes the Armored Divine Beast "Kiba."
{x00}
rows.notes: [jp] = "Chief" (could also be "Boss"). | [editorial] Japanese-English 'mood-maker'; doubled 'apparently' smoothed

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Teddyam
%4■Profile■%1
> A bear Animanoid (beastman) warrior sent from Eternalia, a world in another dimension, to support Kira.
> Teddyam has great fighting strength but is quite defiant, perhaps because an enemy once killed Teddyam's younger sister.
> At first Teddyam clashed with Toya and the other Animanoid warriors, and harshly berated Kira, who could not fully bring out the power of a warrior.
> However, as Kira shows remarkable growth as a warrior and awakens to the power of the Gulkeeva (legendary warrior), Teddyam gradually comes to trust Kira.
> Receiving power from Kira's axe, Teddyam becomes the Armored Divine Beast "Kiba."
{x00}
rows.notes: Glossary gender null and the text has no pronoun, so the name is repeated instead of he/she.

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Rem
%4■Full Name■%1
Dar Rem
%4■Profile■%1
> A leader of the Darknoids, who are the enemies of Toya, Kira and the Animanoid warriors.
> A cold-blooded schemer who will use any means to achieve his ends, he is known by the epithet "Freezing Eyes of Cybele."
> He seems to seek the strongest warrior, the Gulkeeva (legendary warrior), as the one who will fight him and who is meant to kill him.
> To fulfill that wish, he devises various schemes to make Toya awaken as a Gulkeeva, but he feels indignant toward Toya, who cannot fully become one.
> Incidentally, "Dar" is a title for Darknoid warriors.
{x00}
rows.notes: Darknoid romanized; [jp] romanized "Cybele" (not in glossary; "Sibelle" possible). [jp] = "leader" (executive/officer).

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Yun
%4■Full Name■%1
Dar Yun
%4■Profile■%1
> A leader of the Darknoids, who are the enemies of Toya, Kira and the Animanoid warriors.
> In Eternalia, a world in another dimension, she commanded Nosfertia, and was feared as the "Vampire of Gilba" for her fighting strength and merciless way of fighting.
> It was Dar Rem who found her and made her a leader of the invasion of Earthside (the world where Toya and the others live).
> She harbors special feelings for him, but what he wanted was not Dar Yun the "woman," but the "warrior" with the great power of the "Vampire of Gilba."
> Yet she is gradually changing from the "Vampire of Gilba" into a woman...
> Incidentally, "Dar" is a title for Darknoid warriors.
{x00}
rows.notes: [jp] romanized "Nosfertia" (not in glossary; unclear whether a unit or a place -- kept "commanded Nosfertia"). Gilba, Earthside romanized.

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Kazuma
%4■Profile■%1
> A boy with Alter powers who lives in the undeveloped zone outside the redeveloped city of the Lost Ground.
> Where he was born, whether he has any family, even whether Kazuma is his real name -- none of it is certain.
> Since childhood he has survived alone, relying only on his Alter ability.
> He now lives with a girl named Kanami Yuta in a building that was once a clinic.
> Normally he is spaced-out and unreliable.
> He cannot do simple addition, and he does not really understand the value of money either.
> He does go out to work at a ranch with Kanami now and then, but he has almost no motivation and slacks off at every opportunity.
> In short, he is nearly useless when it comes to everyday life, and he constantly relies on Kanami, who is only half his age, to look after him.
> Behind the scenes, however, he teams up with Kunihiko Kimishima and works, fairly recklessly, as an Alter user for hire who takes on any job.
> He tends to be seen as just charging in blindly without thinking, but that is only because he follows his own rules and acts without hesitation.
{x00}
rows.notes: Lost Ground, Alter per official s-CRY-ed English (glossary has Alter Crystal only). | [editorial] stiff opening apposition; awkward 'carries out ... work ... who will do any job'

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Kanami
%4■Full Name■%1
Kanami Yuta
%4■Profile■%1
> A dependable girl who lives with Kazuma.
> Worried about Kazuma, who cannot manage daily life, she devotedly looks after him, making him sandwich lunches, cleaning and so on.
> Since she lives with a housemate who has zero sense of money, she also secretly squirrels away savings.
> Almost every day she dreams -- dreams someone else's dreams -- and she seems to share their feelings, but...
{x00}
rows.notes: [editorial] 'To get by' misread the cause; 'secretly saves up a hidden stash' redundant

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Kimishima
%4■Full Name■%1
Kunihiko Kimishima
%4■Profile■%1
> A small-time punk who is Kazuma's partner in mischief and also his business partner.
> With no Alter ability, he has lived by his wits and his mouth alone.
> He brings in jobs on behalf of Kazuma, who is hot-headed and could not, even charitably, be called smart or savvy.
> He looks like a frivolous, sloppy goof, but he is a man with a surprising sense of responsibility, who can put his own body on the line when needed.
{x00}
rows.notes: [accuracy] [jp]...[jp] = 'even to flatter him you could not say'; 'to put it kindly' reversed the force

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Ryuho
%4■Profile■%1
> A member of HOLY, the anti-Alter-user special unit of HOLD, the armed police organization that keeps order in the Lost Ground.
> He is one of the top Alter users even among HOLY's members, and he is also the eldest son and heir of the Ryu family, the de facto rulers of the Lost Ground.
> He has firm convictions and his own sense of justice, and he is strict with both himself and others.
> He has nearly everything people wish for -- status, wealth, looks, ability and strength of mind -- but he is blind to people's feelings and awkward by nature.
> As a result he gives a cold impression, but he fights out of kindness: he cannot stand by and watch those without Alter powers being trampled and persecuted by the power of Alter users.
> He also has a personal past in which his mother was killed by a mysterious Alter, and he deeply hates Alter criminals who act with impunity.
{x00}

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Scheris
%4■Full Name■%1
Scheris Adjani
%4■Profile■%1
> A member of HOLY, the anti-Alter-user special unit of HOLD, the armed police organization that keeps order in the Lost Ground. She is a former Inner (resident of the undeveloped zone).
> Then again, considering that Alter users are born in the Lost Ground, mostly in its undeveloped zone, it follows naturally that many members of HOLY, a group of Alter users, are former Inners.
> A bright, cheerful girl, she makes it her creed to act true to herself.
> She is experienced for her age and has a mature, pragmatic outlook, but she also has an innocent side, devoted wholeheartedly to Ryuho, who once saved her.
{x00}
rows.notes: [jp] = "Inner" (official s-CRY-ed term; not in glossary). | [editorial] HOLY phrase unified (see 277); dangling modifier (girl -> creed)

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Cougar
%4■Full Name■%1
Straight Cougar
%4■Profile■%1
> A member of HOLY, the anti-Alter-user special unit of HOLD, the armed police organization that keeps order in the Lost Ground.
> His creed is "Speed is power," and even when he talks, he rattles things off at top speed.
> He puts on a frivolous air, but he is a man with a sound, grown-up way of thinking.
> He is fond of Mimori Kiryu and keeps flirting with her, but it never seems to pay off.
> Originally an Inner (resident of the undeveloped zone), he once lived with Kazuma for a time.
> Back then he had a great influence on Kazuma's way of life, and apparently it was also he who gave the Alter its name.
> But once Kazuma was able to stand on his own, Cougar went off alone to the city in search of a "cultured life" and joined HOLY.
> He is oddly well informed about the inner workings of HOLY and the Lost Ground, and he seems to have some secret of his own.
{x00}
rows.notes: [jp]: the source does not say whose Alter; context implies Kazuma's, so "the Alter" kept (not specified). "he went off alone" = Cougar ([jp]), not Kazuma -- context settles it. | [editorial] HOLY phrase unified (see 277); 'he' read as Kazuma -- Cougar named (translator note: Cougar)

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Mimori
%4■Full Name■%1
Mimori Kiryu
%4■Profile■%1
> The daughter of Tadanori Kiryu, the mainland's most powerful figure in the Lost Ground and a financial backer of HOLD.
> Partly because she met Ryuho as a child and was drawn to him, she came to the Lost Ground for the first time in seven years to research Alter abilities, and joined HOLY's science and technology team.
> She is bewildered by how completely Ryuho has changed, yet she still cannot bring herself to leave him.
> Through HOLY's activities she comes face to face with the contradictions and injustices of the Lost Ground and HOLD, and from there she chooses her own path and follows it.
> Though she has a fragile side, she is a girl with inner strength.
{x00}
rows.notes: [jp] romanized "Tadanori Kiryu" (not in glossary).

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Tachibana
%4■Full Name■%1
Asuka Tachibana
%4■Profile■%1
> A B-class member of HOLY, the anti-Alter-user special unit of HOLD, the armed police organization that keeps order in the Lost Ground.
> He is very confident in his own ability and shows off about it.
> On the other hand, he has a fragile side: he is terrified of losing his position as a HOLY member, and of having his life with his girlfriend Cammy destroyed.
> But after meeting Kazuma, even he is inspired by Kazuma's way of life and begins to change.
{x00}
rows.notes: [jp] romanized "Cammy" (not in glossary; "Kyami" possible). | [editorial] HOLY phrase unified (see 277); stiff last sentence smoothed

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Urizane
%4■Profile■%1
> A member of HOLY, the anti-Alter-user special unit of HOLD, the armed police organization that keeps order in the Lost Ground.
> He is a goofy man who is always eating watermelon, but his skill is first-rate.
{x00}
rows.notes: [editorial] HOLY phrase unified (see 277); fragment + 'but' clause given a subject

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Unkei
%4■Profile■%1
> A member of HOLY, the anti-Alter-user special unit of HOLD, the armed police organization that keeps order in the Lost Ground.
> He calls himself an ideal, once-in-a-generation screenwriter with a craftsman's temperament who never loses his own authorial voice... but his actual ability is highly doubtful.
> He has an impressive build, but his combat ability is nothing special.
{x00}
rows.notes: [editorial] garden-path 'unit against Alter users of HOLD' -> machine-library wording 'anti-Alter-user special unit of HOLD'

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Kigetsuki
%4■Full Name■%1
Sou Kigetsuki
%4■Profile■%1
> A member of HOLY, the anti-Alter-user special unit of HOLD, the armed police organization that keeps order in the Lost Ground.
> A cringeworthy man who hates real women, turns his back on reality, and keeps his ideal women, made real with his Alter, at his side at all times.
> A narcissist with strong ambitions and a snide personality.
{x00}
rows.notes: [jp] = "cringeworthy man". Last line kept as a noun phrase like the source (subject is the entry itself). | [editorial] HOLY phrase unified (see 277); trailing participle moved next to its noun

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Shoka
%4■Profile■%1
> A girl created with an Alter as Kigetsuki's "ideal girl."
> Everything down to her personality and habits was set by Kigetsuki, yet she behaves almost as if she had a will of her own.
> Shoka was set up as a younger, little-sister type of girl; she is bright and canny, but is said to have a lonely side too...
> Here one catches a glimpse of Kigetsuki's geeky tastes.
{x00}

%4■Name■%1
Chuka
%4■Profile■%1
> A girl created with an Alter as Kigetsuki's "ideal girl."
> Everything down to her personality and habits was set by Kigetsuki, yet she behaves almost as if she had a will of her own.
> Chuka was set up as a bespectacled honor-student girl; she is a little off and spacey, but is said to make bold moves at times...
> Here one catches a glimpse of Kigetsuki's geeky tastes.
{x00}

%4■Name■%1
Banka
%4■Profile■%1
> A girl created with an Alter as Kigetsuki's "ideal girl."
> Everything down to her personality and habits was set by Kigetsuki, yet she behaves almost as if she had a will of her own.
> Banka was set up as a sexy, big-sister type of woman; she is very experienced and exudes grown-up allure, but is said to have a surprisingly domestic side too...
> Here one catches a glimpse of Kigetsuki's geeky tastes.
{x00}

%4■Name■%1
Mujo
%4■Full Name■%1
Kyoji Mujo
%4■Profile■%1
> An Alter user sent to the Lost Ground at the behest of the mainland, including Tadanori Kiryu, Mimori Kiryu's father.
> Jealous, sly and spiteful by nature.
> Mujo comes from a family that was crushed by the Ryu family, and spent a poor and miserable childhood.
> Because of that, Mujo feels intense envy toward the privileged.
> To fill that inner void, Mujo willingly underwent enhancement and refinement of the Alter ability at a mainland Alter research institution.
> Still not satisfied, Mujo burns with desire for more power, and for authority.
{x00}
rows.notes: Glossary gender null and the text has no pronoun, so the name is repeated instead of he/she. Second paragraph kept as a noun-phrase descriptor (source: [jp]...). | [editorial] 'void in the heart' stiff workaround

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Hayato
%4■Full Name■%1
Hayato Kazami
%4■Profile■%1
> The strongest driver in the world of CF (Cyber Formula), known as the "Ushiwakamaru of the Circuit."
> He debuted at the 10th CF World Grand Prix at 14, the youngest ever, and won the overall championship right away.
> The following year he won for the second year running, shining as champion of the glorious 11th, the "Double One."
> But at the next one, the 12th, he was involved in a collision and a huge crash, and suffered near-fatal injuries.
> There were rumors he would retire, but he made a comeback the following year.
> With all kinds of techniques and the "ZERO Zone," a realm of perception beyond human limits, he has worked many miracles.
> Hayato has run up against wall after wall, and each time he has overcome it with the support of those around him and his girlfriend, Asuka Sugo.
> Honest by nature, he often loses sight of everything around him when it comes to racing.
> Together with Asurada, his ultimate partner, he keeps on racing in order to be true to himself.
{x00}
rows.notes: [jp] = "World Grand Prix" (Cyber Formula season); later bare [jp]N[jp] rendered "the Nth". ZERO Zone, Asurada, Double One per series usage (not in glossary). | [editorial] 'the ultimate partner' -> 'his'

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Asuka
%4■Full Name■%1
Asuka Sugo
%4■Profile■%1
> Hayato Kazami's childhood friend and beloved fiancee.
> She has watched over him from the pit ever since he first began competing in Cyber Formula.
> Hayato so often loses sight of everything around him when it comes to racing that Asuka's feelings toward him have been shaken many times.
> But when Hayato came back from his big crash and resolved to keep racing, Asuka wanted to protect him and set her sights on becoming a doctor.
> Her cooking, which had always been hopeless, has reportedly improved since she began living with Hayato.
{x00}
rows.notes: [editorial] two loosely joined clauses made causal (source: toward Hayato, who...); 'since forever' too casual for reference register

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Randoll
%4■Full Name■%1
Karl Lichter von Randoll
%4■Profile■%1
> A young nobleman known as the "Amadeus of the Circuit," whose driving shows true genius.
> An Austrian aristocrat with both wealth and fame, he has tremendous pride and a sense of money far removed from ordinary people's.
> He was a peerless genius who entered sport after sport and easily took the top spot in each, yet in CF (Cyber Formula) he has still not won the overall championship.
> That does not mean his ability falls short, however; it is merely the result of the carelessness that comes with genius, and a little bad luck.
> He sees Hayato Kazami as his rival, and one reason Randoll, who is also a businessman, still keeps racing is to beat Hayato.
> The scar on his face came from his big crash with Hayato at the 12th, but he has chosen to keep it rather than have it removed.
> He was the first to inherit the Union Saber tradition (?) of the Schumacher goggles.
> Incidentally, his name at that time was Prince Rosenkreuz.
{x00}
rows.notes: The two-line full name joined on one line. Union Saber, Schumacher, Rosenkreuz romanized (not in glossary). The source's "(?)" kept. | [editorial] stiff 'displays driving of genius'; 'left it rather than remove it'

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Grayson
%4■Full Name■%1
George Grayson
%4■Profile■%1
Randoll's butler
{x00}
rows.notes: Source line has no indent and no full stop; kept as a plain line.

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Shinjo
%4■Full Name■%1
Naoki Shinjo
%4■Profile■%1
> An orthodox driver known as the "Young Warrior of the Circuit."
> He stepped up steadily from kart racing to two straight championships in European F3, and then to CF (Cyber Formula).
> Having followed the typical elite path for a racer, he made a much-hyped CF debut and was expected to have a bright future.
> Unfortunately, however, he was overshadowed by drivers of genius who debuted around the same time, such as Hayato, Randoll and Kaga, and he became a driver who was fast, to be sure, but left no impression.
> Mentally fragile, he often took other people's gossip at face value and lost sight of everything around him.
> Just before the start of the 15th he was fired by Aoi, his team, and through a warrior's training journey in America he broke out of his old shell, learned many things, and grew much stronger, changing greatly in both his driving and his heart.
> His desire to win is stronger than anyone's; there is a story from his debut year, the 10th, in which he pushed his machine across the finish line by hand after it stopped just short of the goal.
{x00}
rows.notes: Team [jp] = "Aoi" (romanized; not in glossary).

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Kaga
%4■Full Name■%1
Bleed Kaga
%4■Real Name■%1
Jotaro Kaga
%4■Profile■%1
> One of the strongest drivers in Cyber Formula, Hayato Kazami's greatest rival and best friend.
> Like Hayato, Kaga drives with a genius that comes through in the clutch, but comes from quite a different background, with experience of all kinds of racing, from amateur races to crash races.
> Cheerful and free-spirited by nature, Kaga hates being tied down and is fussy about money.
> When it comes to friends, however, Kaga charges in without a care for personal danger.
> This is probably because Kaga once lost a close friend in an accident during a race they were both in.
> Kaga is also the boss of the Cyber Formula Safety Support System, an organization that protects drivers' safety.
{x00}
rows.notes: Glossary gender null and the text has no pronoun, so the name is repeated instead of he/she. Real name per glossary note. | [accuracy] [jp] = in a race both were in; 'the same race' had no referent | [editorial] name repetition in one sentence reduced

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Osamu
%4■Full Name■%1
Osamu Sugo
%4■Profile■%1
> Asuka's older brother, who leads the Sugo team as its owner and manager.
> He has a habit of nagging and lecturing, and he is well up on the gossip around the circuit.
> He was once a driver who hid his face behind a goggle mask and called himself Knight Schumacher.
> With a near-godlike sense for driving, he earned the epithet "Supersonic Prince" for his flawless precision and overwhelming speed.
> However, he was caught up in a major accident that damaged his optic nerve, and he was forced to retire.
{x00}
rows.notes: Source writes the team as [jp] here and [jp] elsewhere; rendered SUGO here and Sugo elsewhere -- may want unifying. Knight Schumacher romanized. | [editorial] team name unified with the other Cyber Formula entries (Sugo, not SUGO)

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Gudelian
%4■Full Name■%1
Jackie Gudelian
%4■Profile■%1
> A superstar called the "Star Prince" in his home country, America.
> Easily carried away and quick to buy into gossip, he always has a crowd of girls in tow, but in truth he also has a serious side that puts racing first above all else.
> He and the team's manager-driver, Franz Heinel, differ completely in personality and driving style and are always fighting, but they are good rivals who spur each other on.
> He was active in American racing from a young age, and he has won there too.
> On the strength of that record he made a much-hyped Cyber Formula debut, but although he placed near the top, he showed little sign of moving up.
> However, after moving to the team led by Franz Heinel, his former rival, he made rapid progress.
> And at last, at the 14th, he won the glory of his first overall championship.
{x00}
rows.notes: [accuracy] [jp] = easily carried away / flippant, not 'show-off'

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Heinel
%4■Full Name■%1
Franz Heinel
%4■Profile■%1
> Stormzender's team manager, who is not only a top-class driver but also a machine designer.
> As a driver he is known as the "Precision Machine of the Circuit," turning in consistently strong results with thoroughly calculated driving.
> As a machine designer he creates innovative, original machines with flexible thinking, always showing top-class technical skill.
> However, because of his rich talents he is troubled by the difficult choice between being a driver and being a designer.
> Normally cool-headed, he apparently cannot stay that way around Gudelian, and their shouting matches never end.
> On top of that, he also seems to have a weak spot for his younger sister, Lisa Heinel; faced with "Pleeease, big brotherrr!" he cannot keep up his usual sternness.
{x00}
rows.notes: [jp] = "Stormzender" (glossary position notes for Gudelian/Heinel). | [editorial] 'who' attached to Stormzender; 'choice between driver and designer'; 'Always cool-headed ... cannot stay that way' contradiction

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Hiyoshi
%4■Full Name■%1
Akira Hiyoshi
%4■Profile■%1
> The driver who was originally supposed to drive Asurada.
> But because of trouble while Asurada was being delivered to the circuit, Hayato was registered in the driver registration system, and Hiyoshi was removed as the driver.
> Leaving Sugo in despair, he went to Brazil, where his talent was spotted by Pitalia Lope, a former Cyber Formula champion who was working as a team manager, and he made a second debut.
> He is an unremarkable driver who seldom breaks into the top places, but he does his best with the conditions he is given.
{x00}
rows.notes: [jp] romanized "Pitalia Lope" (not in glossary).

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Bootsvorz
%4■Full Name■%1
Edelhi Bootsvorz
%4■Profile■%1
> The oldest active top driver, with a mechanical arm and eye.
> He was Osamu Sugo's teammate in their F1 days.
> He crashed during a test run and injured his left hand and left eye, but he was turned into a cyborg through the power of a shadowy organization and entered Cyber Formula.
> At first he was such a rough driver that he was called "Crusher Bootsvorz," but after the organization pulled out, he began to drive fairly and steadily.
> His driving is unflashy and solid, but that does not mean he is not aiming for the top; he is watching keenly for a chance to seize glory.
{x00}
rows.notes: Source says [jp] (arm) in the first line and [jp] (left hand) later; both kept.

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Claire
%4■Full Name■%1
Claire Fortran
%4■Profile■%1
> A machine designer who worked on the design of Asurada together with Hiroyuki Kazami, Hayato Kazami's father.
> From the 11th, Claire joined the Sugo team in the pit as a staff member.
> An extremely capable mechanic, Claire can spot problems with a machine's condition or its settings precisely and fix them.
> Claire is also skilled at grasping a driver's latent ability and drawing out that potential.
> Claire goes at an easy pace and always wears a carefree smile, but can also say harsh things quite casually.
> Engaged to Osamu Sugo, the Sugo team's manager, Claire can also handle housework perfectly.
> Claire may be a whiz with machines, but behind the wheel of a car always drives at 30 km/h, causing traffic jams.
{x00}
rows.notes: Glossary gender null and the text has no pronoun, so the name is repeated instead of he/she; [jp] rendered "Engaged to" to avoid fiance/fiancee. [jp] romanized "Hiroyuki Kazami" (not in glossary). | [editorial] 'Sugo's manager' read as the person Sugo; subjectless clause after comma

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Miki
%4■Full Name■%1
Miki Jonouchi
%4■Profile■%1
> Less a team mechanic than Naoki Shinjo's personal mechanic.
> Up to the 13th CF (Cyber Formula) Grand Prix, Miki was chief mechanic of the Sugo team.
> From the following one, the 14th, Miki moved to Aoi, Shinjo's team, and from then on was always at his side.
> Miki takes great pride in being a mechanic, and makes it a creed to bring the machine to its best condition personally.
> Not a natural genius, Miki is a hard worker who hates to lose, and gets the machine close to perfect even at reckless personal risk.
> Miki has feelings for Shinjo, who seems a kindred spirit, and when he was fired from his team and went to America for a warrior's training journey, Miki supported him in body and mind as his personal mechanic.
> Through that training with Shinjo, Miki also seems to have grown a notch as a person, with stronger leadership of the pit crew and even deeper trust from the staff.
{x00}
rows.notes: Glossary gender null and the text has no pronoun for Miki, so the name is repeated. Source typos [jp] (for [jp]), [jp] (for [jp]) and [jp] read as Naoki Shinjo / Cyber Formula. | [editorial] stiff opening; '13th CF' lacked a noun; 'by hand'; 'Miki's own safety' repetition

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Kyoko
%4■Full Name■%1
Kyoko Aoi
%4■Profile■%1
> The daughter of the president of Aoi Motor Industries, one of the world's leading automakers, and the owner of the company's CF (Cyber Formula) team.
> She tends to be seen as a strong-willed, strict, win-at-all-costs type, but her love for her team is second to none, and she is set on winning the series with the staff who have shared the ups and downs with her.
> Just before the 15th, because of the team's poor results, she was demoted from owner to vice-president, but even after such humiliation she kept on watching over the team.
> She is especially soft on Shinjo, whom she picked herself, and she once even defended him by staking her own position.
> In high school, as the ace of the kyudo archery club, she was nicknamed the "She-Leopard of the Beach," and because of that she was strangely misunderstood at the kart race during a company trip.
{x00}
rows.notes: [jp] = "Aoi Motor Industries" (not in glossary). [jp] = "She-Leopard of the Beach" ([jp] could also be a place name, e.g. Yokohama).

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Henri
%4■Full Name■%1
Henri Claytor
%4■Profile■%1
> The other driver on the Sugo team, alongside Hayato Kazami.
> At the 13th he won the overall championship at the age of just 15.
> He has something of a split personality, treating people very differently depending on who they are.
> From early childhood he received elite training from his father, a former racer, and raced toward his father's dream: becoming the youngest overall champion in Cyber Formula history.
> However, every part of that dream had already been achieved by Hayato, and in despair, Henri's father began to abuse him.
> As a result Henri came to hate Hayato, and at the 13th his acting skill was used to devastating effect to bring Hayato down.
> But through their battles he came to know Hayato's character, and as he kept watching Hayato drive, his hatred turned into admiration.
> After that, his admiration for Hayato gradually began to go astray, heading in a dangerous direction...
{x00}
rows.notes: [editorial] 'fulfilled that dream entirely' unclear (Hayato had already achieved it)

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Phil
%4■Full Name■%1
Phil Fritz
%4■Profile■%1
> He entered Cyber Formula from the 15th, and in his debut race he won from pole position, only the second driver in history to do so.
> His speed was so overwhelming that even Hayato Kazami, the strongest driver, could not get near him.
> But that speed was merely the product of a drug called "alpha-Neuro," which greatly boosted his reflexes and numbed his fear of speed so that he would drive exactly as the computer instructed.
> Of course, giving this drug is a violation of the regulations and also harms the user's body, but he accepted Nagumo's offer fully aware of that.
> He did so out of a strong longing to be a top driver, which he still could not give up even though he understood his ability was not that great.
> He is shy and not good with words, but his love of racing is second to none.
{x00}
rows.notes: α[jp] = "alpha-Neuro" (ASCII; glossary position note). Pronoun "he" per the source's [jp] (glossary gender null). [jp] rendered "won from pole position".

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Nagumo
%4■Full Name■%1
Kyoshiro Nagumo
%4■Profile■%1
> The owner of Aoi, who took over from Kyoko Aoi after she was held responsible for the team's poor results and demoted.
> Bringing Al-Zard, completed by his own development team, and Phil, its dedicated driver, he promised victory.
> His older brother once developed machines together with Hayato Kazami's father, aiming at "the fusion of man and machine."
> But after parting ways with the development team over differing ideas, the brother completed "Ogre."
> However, although that machine had extremely high performance, there was no driver who could meet its demands, and no fewer than two drivers died in testing.
> In despair, his brother took his own life.
> To prove his brother's ideals right, he detuned that machine somewhat and, by using drugs to turn the driver into a component of the machine, completed Al-Zard.
> It seems he became Aoi's owner in order to race it.
> His father, whose auto-parts company had been taken over by Aoi Motors, killed himself.
> The reason he still chose Aoi is apparently that he had known Kyoko Aoi since before becoming owner, and had feelings for her.
{x00}
rows.notes: [jp] = "Al-Zard", [jp] ([jp]) = "Ogre" (series usage; not in glossary). [jp] kept as "as many as two". | [accuracy] order restored: held responsible -> demoted ([jp]) | [editorial] 'as many as two' unidiomatic for the emphatic [jp]

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Luisa
%4■Full Name■%1
Marie Albert Luisa
%4■Profile■%1
> The only active female driver in Cyber Formula.
> Very strong-willed, she hates being treated as a woman at the circuit.
> A racing lover to the core, she has experience not only in all kinds of races but even as a course marshal.
> Through much hardship and effort she has steadily built up her skill; she has worked hard to get where she is.
{x00}

%4■Name■%1
Natsumi
%4■Full Name■%1
Natsumi Mizuki
%4■Profile■%1
> A fourth-grader at Yumegaoka Elementary School.
> Cheerful and lively, and popular in class.
> The day before leaving for London because of the parents' work, Natsumi meets Mirai -- Natsumi's own child, time-slipped from 15 years in the future -- and decides to raise the baby.
> Natsumi can be lonely and clingy, but gradually grows up through life with Mirai and with Aunt Izumi.
{x00}
rows.notes: Glossary gender null for Natsumi and Mirai and the text has no pronoun, so names are repeated instead of he/she (wording is heavy; an editor may prefer "she" if gender is confirmed). Second paragraph kept subjectless as in the source descriptor. [jp] romanized "Yumegaoka". | [editorial] name repetition: 'Izumi, Natsumi's aunt' -> 'Aunt Izumi'

rows.en:
%4■Name■%1
Mirai
%4■Profile■%1
> Natsumi's baby, who has time-slipped from 15 years in the future.
> An energetic child whose boundless activity often causes trouble for those nearby, but who grows up healthy, loved by Natsumi and the others.
{x00}

%4■Name■%1
Izumi
%4■Full Name■%1
Izumi Shimamura
%4■Profile■%1
> Natsumi's aunt, who came to look after the Mizuki house while the family is away.
> An aspiring manga artist who hates dogs and babies.
> She usually draws nothing but "violent stuff," but she has a kind side, drawing heartwarming manga for Natsumi and Mirai.
{x00}

%4■Name■%1
Eji
